The answer depends on the type of public school in question, as the retrieved evidence covers multiple distinct milestones in U.S. public education. The first public school in America overall was the Boston Latin School, which opened on April 23, 1635, in Boston, Massachusetts [d8]. According to multiple sources, this school is considered the very first public school in what is now the United States, founded when a handful of students met in the private home of a headmaster [d7][d9]. Separately, the first public high school in the U.S. — the English Classical School (later renamed the English High School in 1824) — was established in Boston in 1821, serving working-class boys who did not plan to attend college [d5][d1]. Additionally, the first public normal school (for teacher training) was founded in 1839 in Lexington, Massachusetts [d3].
